name: Akash-NG (New Generation) Surface-to-Air Missile

what_it_is.prose: The Akash-NG (New Generation) is a DRDO-developed medium-range Surface-to-Air Missile system, the latest variant of the Akash SAM family. The original Akash Mk-I (25 km range, 1990s design) was inducted by the Indian Army and IAF starting in 2014; Akash Prime (high-altitude optimised) was first tested in 2021; Akash-NG extends the range to 80+ km and altitude to 18 km, and introduces an indigenous active radar seeker — a significant upgrade from the passive seeker on the original Akash. The system can intercept fighters, helicopters, UAVs, cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles. DRDO laboratories involved include LRDE (radar), RCI (seeker and guidance), and R&DE(E) (launcher). Production agencies are BEL (Rajendra-NG radar, C4I system) and BDL (missile assembly). The Akash system as a whole has aggregate orders exceeding ₹30,000 crore across the Indian Army and IAF, with BEL and BDL as prime contractors. Akash-NG has undergone multiple successful test firings in 2023-2025 at the Integrated Test Range, Chandipur. The Akashteer Air Defence Control & Reporting System, battle-proven during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, integrates Akash-family SAMs with BEL's C4I infrastructure.

faq.question: What is the difference between Akash Mk-I, Akash Prime, and Akash-NG?
faq.answer: Akash Mk-I is the original 25 km range SAM inducted from 2014. Akash Prime is a high-altitude optimised variant first tested in 2021. Akash-NG (New Generation) extends the range to 80+ km and altitude to 18 km, and introduces an indigenous active radar seeker — a significant upgrade from the passive seeker on the original Akash. All three are DRDO-designed with BEL and BDL as productionisers.

faq.question: Was the Akash system used in Operation Sindoor?
faq.answer: Yes. The Akashteer Air Defence Control & Reporting System, which integrates Akash-family SAMs with BEL's C4I infrastructure, was battle-proven during Operation Sindoor in May 2025. PIB confirmed this in a press release dated 16 May 2025. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh subsequently credited both Akash and BrahMos as having been proven in combat during the operation.

faq.question: Has Akash been exported?
faq.answer: Armenia was reported in 2025 as the first export customer for the Akash Mk-I system. The export demonstrated Indian SAM capability on the global market, alongside BrahMos exports to the Philippines ($375M, 2022) and Indonesia (~$450M, 2026). Akash-NG export potential has not yet been articulated but is expected to follow once domestic orders are fulfilled.
